title: Long live cash: why Japan is in no hurry to go cashless

words.note: 这是祝愿式的欢呼：Long live the King! = 国王万岁！live 用原形、不加 s（古老的祈愿句式留下的写法）。标题借它来调侃现金，半开玩笑：现金万岁。反过来，要喊“打倒……”可以说 Down with …!
words.ctx: Long live cash: why Japan is in no hurry to go cashless

ex.en: Crowds in the square shouted, “[[Long live]] the republic!”
ex.zh: 广场上的人群高喊：“共和国万岁！”

ex.en: The banner read “[[Long live]] the underdog!”
ex.zh: 横幅上写着：“弱者万岁！”

words.expr: be in no hurry to do sth
words.note: no 加强否定，in no hurry 比 not in a hurry 语气更重。常见搭配：be in no hurry to do sth / be in no hurry for sth。对比 in a hurry（匆忙、着急）。标题说日本“不急着”告别现金，正文里的 unhurried 讲的是同一种从容。

ex.en: I am [[in no hurry to]] leave, so take your time.

ex.zh: 市议会并不急着按这份报告行动。

words.note: go + 形容词 = 变成某种状态：go bald（秃了）、go quiet（安静下来）、go viral（走红）。cashless 由 cash + -less（没有……的）构成，和 jobless、homeless 同一个造词法。标题里是 go cashless，第 4 句里变成 going cashless（介词 into 后面接动名词）。

words.note: 《经济学人》常用 the rich world 指发达经济体，对应 the poor world / the developing world。much of the rich world = 富裕国家的大部分地区（much of + the + 名词 = ……的大部分）。
words.ctx: In much of the rich world, tapping a phone has replaced fumbling for coins.

ex.en: Populations are ageing fast across [[the rich world]].
ex.zh: 整个富裕国家的人口都在迅速老龄化。

ex.en: Few jobs in [[the rich world]] are untouched by software.
ex.zh: 在富裕国家，几乎没有哪种工作不受软件影响。

words.zh: 轻点；（用手机、卡）碰一下支付
words.note: tap 本义是轻轻拍、轻轻敲。用手机或银行卡在读卡器上轻轻一碰就付款，英语里就叫 tap（tap to pay）。tapping a phone 是动名词短语，作 has replaced 的主语，对比后面的 fumbling for coins：一边轻巧，一边笨拙。
words.ctx: In much of the rich world, tapping a phone has replaced fumbling for coins.

ex.en: Just [[tap]] your card on the reader to pay.

ex.en: She [[tapped]] the screen twice to zoom in.

words.note: survive 最常见的意思是“活下来”，也可以指旧事物、旧习惯留存下来：the old habit survives = 老习惯没有消失。名词 survival，幸存者 survivor。

words.note: wave 最常见的意思是“挥手”，但 wave sth at sb/sth 是手里拿着某样东西，朝着某人或某物晃动。这里是拿手机对着读卡器一晃就付款，动作轻松随意。

words.note: 这里的 see 不是“看见”，而是“看待、理解”：see A as B（把 A 看成 B）、see things differently（看法不同）。it 指上一句里“像时间胶囊”的印象：游客觉得这是怀旧，而官员不这么看。

words.ctx: Officials have long tried to nudge people along.

words.ctx: Japan's workforce is shrinking, and every hour a shopkeeper spends counting the till costs more each year.

ex.en: The cashier counted the [[till]] at closing time.
ex.zh: 收银员在打烊时清点了收银抽屉。

ex.en: Someone had taken money from the [[till]].
ex.zh: 有人从收银抽屉里拿走了钱。

words.note: handle 本义是用手拿、摆弄，常引申为“处理、应付、经手”：handle complaints / handle money。名词 handle 是把手、柄。Handling cash 是动名词短语作主语，指经手现金的全过程：收、数、存、运。
words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: Banks must [[handle]] customer data with care.
ex.zh: 银行必须小心地处理客户数据。

ex.en: She [[handles]] the accounts for three small firms.
ex.zh: 她替三家小公司经手账目。

cloze.after: cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.
cloze.szh: 处理现金是一笔隐形开支：纸币要清点、存入银行、用运钞车运来运去，还得有人把那些取款机一直补满。

words.note: hidden 是 hide 的过去分词作形容词：藏起来的、看不见的。hidden cost / hidden expense / hidden fee = 表面上没算进去的成本。冒号后面的内容就是对它的解释：notes must be counted, banked and ferried about ...
words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: Parking is often a [[hidden expense]] of owning a car.
ex.zh: 停车往往是养车时隐形的开支。

ex.en: Cheap flights can come with [[hidden expenses]], such as baggage fees.
ex.zh: 廉价机票可能附带隐性开支，比如行李费。

words.note: bank 除了名词“银行”，还有动词义：把钱存进银行，尤其指商家把当天的收入存入账户。notes must be counted, banked and ferried about：三个被动动词并列，依次是清点、存入、运送，写出了现金要经手的流程。
words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: The shop owner [[banks]] the takings every evening.
ex.zh: 店主每天晚上把营业收入存进银行。

ex.en: She [[banked]] the cheque on her way to work.
ex.zh: 她在上班路上把支票存进了银行。

words.note: ferry 的本义是名词“渡轮、摆渡”（take the ferry = 坐渡轮），作动词时指像渡轮一样来回运送人或物。about = 到处、来回（英式，美式多用 around）：ferry sth about / around。ferried 是过去分词，在 must be counted, banked and ferried about 里构成被动语态；这里是说现金要被一趟趟地运来运去。
words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: Minibuses [[ferry]] guests between the hotel and the beach.
ex.zh: 小巴在酒店和海滩之间接送客人。

ex.en: Volunteers [[ferried]] supplies to the village by boat.
ex.zh: 志愿者们用船把物资运到村子里。

ex.en: Parents spend their weekends [[ferrying]] children about.
ex.zh: 父母们把周末都花在开车接送孩子上。

words.note: armour = 盔甲、装甲，armoured = 披着装甲的、防弹的；an armoured van 就是专门押运现金的防弹车，也叫 security van。armoured 是英式拼写，美式是 armored（同理 colour / color、labour / labor）。van 是厢式货车。要用这样的车来运现金，说明现金的处理链条又长又贵。
words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: Guards loaded the cash into an [[armoured van]].
ex.zh: 警卫把现金装进了运钞车。

ex.en: Two [[armoured vans]] were parked outside the bank.
ex.zh: 有两辆运钞车停在银行外面。

words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: I need to [[top up]] my travel card.
ex.zh: 我得给交通卡充值。

ex.en: The nurse [[topped up]] the water jug.
ex.zh: 护士把水壶重新加满了。

words.note: 这里的 take money 是“收款”，不是“拿走钱”：商家向顾客 take money = 收到顾客付的钱。the cheapest way to take money = 成本最低的收款方式。同类用法：take payment、take cards（接受刷卡）。对比：take money out = 取钱。
words.ctx: Shops and banks are beginning to realise that the cheapest way to take money is the one with the fewest humans involved.

ex.en: The stall [[takes money]] only in cash.
ex.zh: 这个摊位只收现金。

ex.en: Small shops find it hard to [[take money]] by card.
ex.zh: 小店觉得刷卡收款很麻烦。

cloze.before: Shops and banks are beginning to realise that the cheapest way to
cloze.after: money is the one with the fewest humans involved.
cloze.szh: 商店和银行开始意识到，最便宜的收款方式，是牵涉的人最少的那一种。

words.note: with + 名词 + 过去分词 = 在……被……的情况下，表示伴随的状态：with the fewest humans involved = 在牵涉的人最少的情况下。fewest 是 few 的最高级，修饰可数名词（不可数用 least）。the one 代指前面的 way。作者特意写 humans 而不是 staff 或 people，带点冷幽默：最便宜的办法，就是把人拿掉。
words.ctx: Shops and banks are beginning to realise that the cheapest way to take money is the one with the fewest humans involved.

ex.en: Keep the plan simple, with as few people [[involved]] as possible.
ex.zh: 计划要简单，尽量少牵涉人。

ex.en: Any job [[involving]] heavy machinery requires training.
ex.zh: 凡是涉及重型机械的工作都要经过培训。

words.ctx: None of this makes Japan's attachment to cash irrational.

ex.en: Her [[attachment to]] the old village never faded.
ex.zh: 她对老村子的依恋从未淡去。

ex.en: Voters' [[attachment to]] their local hospital is strong.
ex.zh: 选民们对本地医院的感情很深。

cloze.before: None of this makes Japan's
cloze.after: to cash irrational.
cloze.szh: 这一切都不会让日本人对现金的依恋变得不理性。

words.note: ir- 是否定前缀（im- / in- / ir- / il- 同一类），irrational = not rational。它和副标题里的 rational 前后呼应：作者说日本人依恋现金并不是不理性的。同类词：irregular、irrelevant、irresponsible。
words.ctx: None of this makes Japan's attachment to cash irrational.

ex.en: A fear of flying is [[irrational]], but common.
ex.zh: 怕坐飞机并不理性，但很常见。

ex.en: It would be [[irrational]] to ignore the warning signs.
ex.zh: 无视这些警告信号是不理性的。

cloze.before: None of this makes Japan's attachment to cash
cloze.szh: 这一切都不会让日本人对现金的依恋变得不理性。

words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

ex.en: I'll [[stick with]] the plan until it clearly fails.
ex.zh: 在计划明显行不通之前，我会坚持用它。

ex.en: Many fans [[stuck with]] the team through the bad years.
ex.zh: 许多球迷在那些低谷的年头也一直支持这支球队。

cloze.before: People
cloze.after: with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.
cloze.szh: 人们会坚持用管用的东西，而改用新办法的成本，对那些能从中获益的人来说，很容易被忽略。

words.zh: 转换成本；改用新办法的代价
words.note: switching 是 switch（改用、转换）的 -ing 形式，在介词 of 后作动名词。the cost of switching = 转换成本，经济学里常说 switching costs：从一种产品或习惯换到另一种，所付出的时间、金钱和精力。这正是日本人继续用现金的一个原因，而推动改变的人容易忽略它。
words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

ex.en: Many people stay with their bank because [[the cost of switching]] seems high.
ex.zh: 许多人一直用原来的银行，因为换银行的成本看起来很高。

ex.en: [[The cost of switching]] to a new system is easy to underestimate.
ex.zh: 换用新系统的成本很容易被低估。

cloze.before: People stick with what works, and the cost of

cloze.szh: 人们会坚持用管用的东西，而改用新办法的成本，对那些能从中获益的人来说，很容易被忽略。

words.note: overlook 还有“俯瞰”的意思：a hotel overlooking the sea。
words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

ex.en: It is easy to [[overlook]] small errors in a long report.
ex.zh: 在一份长报告里，很容易忽略小错误。

ex.en: The committee [[overlooked]] an important detail.
ex.zh: 委员会漏掉了一个重要的细节。

words.note: 对应说法：stand to lose（有可能受损）。
words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

ex.en: Exporters [[stand to gain]] from a weaker currency.
ex.zh: 货币走弱，出口商有可能受益。

ex.en: Who [[stands to gain]] most from the merger?
ex.zh: 这次合并，谁可能获益最多？

words.note: give way (to sth)：（对……）让步；英式里也指“给别的车辆让路”。
words.ctx: Habits rarely give way because someone has made a persuasive case; they do so when the old way becomes more expensive for those who set the price.

ex.en: The old rules finally [[gave way]] to a simpler system.
ex.zh: 旧规定终于让位给了一套更简单的制度。

ex.en: Her anger [[gave way]] to sadness.
ex.zh: 她的愤怒渐渐变成了悲伤。

cloze.before: Habits rarely
cloze.after: way because someone has made a persuasive case; they do so when the old way becomes more expensive for those who set the price.
cloze.szh: 习惯很少是因为有人提出了有说服力的论证才让步；它们让步，是在旧方式对那些定价的人变得更贵的时候。

words.note: 常见变化：make a strong case for sth（为……提出有力的论证）。
words.ctx: Habits rarely give way because someone has made a persuasive case; they do so when the old way becomes more expensive for those who set the price.

ex.en: Lawyers [[make a case]] on behalf of their clients.
ex.zh: 律师替当事人陈述理由。

ex.en: The author [[makes a case]] for slower, deeper reading.
ex.zh: 作者为更慢、更深入的阅读提出了论证。

words.note: set 是不规则动词，原形、过去式、过去分词都是 set；这里的 who set the price 是一般现在时。set the price = 定价，掌握定价权。those who set the price 指商家和银行，而不是付钱的顾客：旧办法对定价的人变贵的时候，习惯才会改。
words.ctx: Habits rarely give way because someone has made a persuasive case; they do so when the old way becomes more expensive for those who set the price.

ex.en: Sellers, not buyers, usually [[set the price]].
ex.zh: 通常是卖方而不是买方来定价。

ex.en: The regulator will [[set the price]] of electricity this winter.
ex.zh: 监管机构将在今年冬天为电价定价。

words.note: 也可以写成 stand-off；《经济学人》多写 standoff。
words.ctx: Until then, the bakery queue will remain a quiet standoff between two ways of paying.

ex.en: The strike ended a six-week [[standoff]] between the union and the firm.
ex.zh: 罢工结束了工会与公司之间长达六周的僵持。

ex.en: A tense [[standoff]] followed at the border.
ex.zh: 边境上随后出现了一场紧张的对峙。
